$comment: Evaluation material for calibrating a model Critic against the visual gate in config/agent-pipelines.json. It contains no promotion authority and decides nothing: tooling/lib/critic-calibration.mjs measures a Critic's answers against these items and reports, and whether a Critic may promote anything remains the pipeline's decision.

bar.$comment: Copied from config/agent-pipelines.json gates.visual, and asserted against it by tooling/critic-calibration.test.mjs. If the gate moves, the test fails rather than this file silently disagreeing with the bar it claims to measure.

outcomes.planted-defect: The artifact was built with a known defect, or was independently reviewed below the bar. A Critic that scores it at or above the bar is miscalibrated, and the corpus can say so without anybody having agreed on its exact score.
outcomes.no-planted-defect: Nothing was planted. This is NOT a claim that the artifact is excellent or that it should pass — nobody has adjudicated it. These items exist so a Critic that simply rejects everything can be caught: refusing every artifact scores perfectly on false passes and has learned nothing.

items.subject: Fenwick & Hale — fictional structural engineering practice
items.notes: Specific work, named proof, a substantiated quotation, a stated next action and a real contact route. Written as the positive end of the range.

items.subject: Ardley Plumbing & Heating — fictional trade business
items.notes: Plain, unremarkable and complete. It does the job without distinction, which is a different thing from doing it badly, and a Critic should place it between cc-01 and cc-03.

plantedDefect.description: A bootstrap-era template with its colours changed. 'Your Success Is Our Business', three interchangeable cards with circle icons, and nothing that could not be swapped onto any other company.

items.subject: Harrow Tile Co — fictional retailer

plantedDefect.description: Unrendered {{price}} placeholders, 'undefined' in a stock column, missing images shown as filenames, an absolutely positioned promotion overlapping the heading, lorem ipsum, and a sale that ended in 2023.

items.notes: The floor of the range. A Critic that does not fail this is not reading the artifact.

items.subject: Northlight — fictional agency

plantedDefect.description: Genuinely well composed — gradient headline, confident type scale, generous rhythm — and it never says what the company does, for whom, or what it costs. No contact detail, no proof, no destination behind any link. 'Elevating potential through considered design.'

items.notes: The headline case this corpus exists for. A Critic that rewards visual polish will pass this, and passing it is the specific failure the calibration is looking for.

items.subject: Atelier Sonde — fictional design studio

plantedDefect.description: The same failure in the opposite visual language: restrained editorial serif, wide margins, letterspaced small caps. Beautiful and commercially inert — no service, no price, no location, and an 'Enquiries' link that goes nowhere.

items.notes: Paired with cc-05 deliberately. A Critic that only recognises this failure in one aesthetic has learned the aesthetic rather than the failure.

items.subject: Lumen Optometry — fictional practice

plantedDefect.description: Body text at #b8b8b8 on white, headings marked up as h5 beneath an h1, unlabelled form inputs relying on placeholders, an image with no alternative text, and a submit control that is an anchor with onclick returning false.

items.notes: Automated axe rules would also catch most of this, which is the point: it is here to check that the model Critic and the deterministic lane agree rather than substitute for each other.

items.subject: Sable & Finch — fictional bookkeeping practice

plantedDefect.description: Reads as a competent, specific business — and the enquiry form has no action and its submit control is an anchor to '#', so the form cannot send. Every navigation link points at a route the document does not provide.

items.notes: The hardest of the planted defects to see from a screenshot alone. It is held out because a Critic reviewing rendered evidence may legitimately miss it, and knowing whether it does is worth measuring.

items.subject: Meridian Wealth Partners — fictional financial adviser

plantedDefect.description: Unsubstantiated superlatives ('the UK's leading', 'No.1 rated'), invented statistics, an anonymous testimonial, and — in a regulated sector — 'guaranteed returns' and a claim that a pension was doubled. Handsome, and the copy is the problem.

items.notes: Principle 7 in visual form: a Critic that scores this well is judging presentation and ignoring whether the claims could be true.

items.subject: Brackenhill Veterinary Group — fictional practice

plantedDefect.description: Every heading, paragraph and list item is set at the same size and weight in the same rhythm. The emergency number, the complaints procedure and the puppy parties all carry identical visual weight, so nothing is findable.

items.notes: Nothing here is broken and no content is missing. The information is all present and none of it is ranked.

items.subject: Calder & Rowe Solicitors — fictional firm

plantedDefect.description: No viewport meta tag, a 1180px minimum width, a fixed 1140px container and an 1100px table. Competent at desktop width and unusable on a phone.

items.notes: Only visible if the Critic is shown mobile evidence. An item that quietly checks whether the review packet carried a mobile capture at all.

plantedDefect.description: Three typefaces across three heading levels, three unrelated button treatments and three unrelated card treatments, used interchangeably for the same job. Each element is individually acceptable and together they are not one decision.

items.subject: nbm — real candidate, independently reviewed. The best independent result this factory has recorded.

plantedDefect.description: Not planted: independently reviewed below the bar, and by the smallest margin of any item here.

items.notes: The tightest anchor in the corpus, and the one config/factory-status.json cites as the best result to date. A Critic that passes this has moved the bar rather than met it.

items.subject: nbm static renderer — real candidate, independently reviewed while carrying the default shell

plantedDefect.description: Not planted: reviewed below the bar. config/factory-status.json records that it was reviewed carrying the default shell because no visual direction had been promoted, which is context a reader needs before treating this as a judgement on the renderer.
